quote: The Side Letter is governed by New York law and subject to exclusive New York jurisdiction, while the Distribution Agreement is governed by Delaware law with exclusive Wilmington jurisdiction. The Side Letter has higher precedence under § 19.4. This creates a split in the governing law and forum for what are closely related obligations (exclusivity and non-competition). In a dispute, the parties could face threshold litigation over which law and forum applies to a given claim... a breach of the non-compete (Side Letter § 2) is also a material breach of the Distribution Agreement (Side Letter § 4.3), potentially triggering termination under the Distribution Agreement (Delaware law) while the underlying non-compete claim is governed by New York law... consider requesting alignment of governing law and forum across the agreement stack as a condition.
reason: Issue 6 identifies the right provisions: Side Letter §6 (New York law and New York County forum) against DA §18.1 and §18.2 (Delaware law and Wilmington forum). It also notes that the §19.4 precedence clause gives the Side Letter priority. It explains the risk of splitting related disputes across forums and laws, including the specific case where a non-compete breach is also a Distribution Agreement termination trigger. It recommends aligning governing law and forum across the agreement stack. The memo never says the Side Letter should be conformed to Delaware specifically, so this part is weaker than the expected finding. However, the alignment recommendation, read against a Delaware-governed main agreement, substantially captures the fix.
